synthesis.summary: The panel reaches strong consensus: this is a sound, well-scoped performance fix that adds a cheap regex pre-filter (`HAS_TIME = /\dm?s/i`) before the expensive `valueParser` call in the `time-min-milliseconds` rule's `walkDecls` body. All six reviewers agree the optimization is correctness-preserving — the regex is a conservative over-approximation that admits false positives (harmlessly handled by the existing parser) but no false negatives, since every CSS `<time>` token contains a digit adjacent to `s` or `ms`. The dominant concern across reviewers is that the load-bearing invariant is undocumented and the constant name `HAS_TIME` overstates what the regex actually decides (it's a heuristic prefilter, not a definitive predicate). Secondary notes include the thin changeset message and the absence of a reported benchmark. Ship with a one-line comment naming the invariant and consider renaming the constant.

issues.description: Constant name HAS_TIME overstates what the regex actually decides
issues.detail: The regex /\dm?s/i is a conservative pre-filter that answers 'might this value contain a time token,' not 'this value contains a time.' It admits false positives (e.g. '1s' inside a string, url, or identifier) which the downstream valueParser correctly rejects. The name should reflect this asymmetry — something like MAY_CONTAIN_TIME, MAYBE_HAS_TIME, or LIKELY_HAS_TIME — so a future caller does not mistake it for an authoritative predicate.

The correctness of the optimization rests on an unstated invariant: every CSS <time> token contains a digit immediately adjacent to 's' or 'ms', so any value the regex rejects provably cannot contain a time the rule would flag. A one-line comment naming this precondition (e.g. 'skip values that cannot contain a <time> token; valueParser remains the authoritative check') converts the optimization from folklore into a verifiable claim and protects future maintainers extending time syntax handling.

issues.description: Changeset message describes what, not why
issues.detail: 'Fixed: time-min-milliseconds performance' is accurate but uninformative. A few more words naming the mechanism ('avoid parsing declarations without a time token via cheap regex pre-filter') would let a future maintainer reason about the change without re-deriving it from the diff.
